raw_response:
I am 54 years old and I never went to school, but I have farmed this land in Quzhou County since I was a young girl. My family has 8 mu, and every year I do what my mother taught me: plant winter wheat in October and then summer maize right after we cut the wheat in early June. I cannot read the labels, but I know which seeds work because I watch my neighbors. I buy the improved wheat variety and the denghai hybrid maize from the village shop — they grow strong and the grain buyer pays a fair price. For the wheat, I rotary till the soil and put down about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before sowing, then spread urea when the wheat turns green in spring. There is no time to till for the maize; we plant it directly into the wheat stubble the same week we harvest. I irrigate the wheat four times — once in winter so it does not freeze, and three more times in spring when the dry wind comes. The maize gets water twice, right after planting and when the tassels come out. I spray for weeds and insects about three times for each crop. It costs money, but losing half the crop would cost more. If the weather is kind, I expect about 550 kg per mu from the wheat and 600 kg per mu from the maize.
